channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek Senators Discuss Cooperation with UK, Irish, and Russian Parliamentarians
item.description: During the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, Uzbek senators met with delegations from the UK, Ireland, and Russia. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral relations, inter-parliamentary cooperation, and exploring joint projects in areas like IT, agriculture, and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Automatic Childcare Allowance for Working Mothers
item.description: Uzbekistan is launching a new automatic childcare allowance for working mothers, funded by the State Social Insurance Fund. The benefit will be paid until the child turns one year old, without requiring applications or additional documents, aiming to provide financial support and compensate for lost income.

item.title: Global Movement Leader Praises Uzbekistan's Youth Focus and Global Leadership
item.description: Asmita Satyarthi, Director-General of the Global Movement for Compassion, commended Uzbekistan's global leadership and its focus on supporting young parliamentarians at a conference in Samarkand. She highlighted the importance of strengthening democratic values and human rights.

item.title: Five EU Nations Agree on Deportation Centers for Irregular Migrants
item.description: Denmark, Austria, Germany, the Netherlands, and Greece have agreed on a common model for deportation centers to negotiate with non-EU countries. The first agreement is expected by 2027, with potential partners like Uganda and Rwanda being discussed. These centers will house asylum seekers whose applications were rejected and cannot be returned to their home countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Approves Digital Som Launch and Blockchain Development
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov chaired a meeting on virtual assets and blockchain, discussing market development and international cooperation. Plans include a pilot launch of the digital som by late 2026 and full implementation by 2027. The National Agency for Virtual Assets was tasked with preparing regulatory acts within three months.

item.title: Tallest Bridge on China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway to be Built in Suzak
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport announced the construction of the tallest bridge on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway in Suzak district, Jalal-Abad region. The bridge over the Koch-Alat River will be 956.67 meters long and 122 meters high. Construction began in December 2024.

item.title: Oybek Kaimxodjayev Appointed Head of Khorezm Region Internal Affairs Directorate
item.description: Lieutenant Colonel Oybek Abdukarimovich Kaimxodjayev has been appointed as the head of the Internal Affairs Directorate for the Khorezm region. He previously served as the head of the Internal Affairs Department for Yashnobod district in Tashkent city since June 2021.

item.title: Russian General Accused of Bombing Kyiv Children's Hospital Shot Dead
item.description: A Russian general, accused of striking a children's hospital in Kyiv, has been shot and killed. The general was admitted to the hospital in critical condition and later transferred to Moscow for treatment.

item.title: UN States Israel 'Deliberately' Killed Palestinian Children and Tortured Them
item.description: The UN reports that Israel has deliberately killed Palestinian children and subjected them to torture. Further details are available in the full report.

item.title: Osh police detain repeat drunk driver stripped of license
item.description: A 36-year-old man in Osh will face trial for driving under the influence again after being previously stripped of his license for two years. He was stopped by patrol officers driving his Lexus 470 while intoxicated, a condition confirmed by medical examination.

item.title: New head appointed for Khorezm region police department
item.description: Oybek Kaimxodjayev has been appointed as the new head of the Khorezm region's Internal Affairs Directorate. Prior to this appointment, he served as the head of the Internal Affairs Bodies Coordination Department for the Yashnobod district of Tashkent city.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan envoy suggests visa fee for US citizens
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to the US, Edil Baisalov, proposed introducing a visa fee of $100-$200 for US citizens. He believes this measure would not deter American tourists and could help balance visa requirements, citing stricter US visa policies for Kyrgyz citizens.

item.title: UNICEF reports nearly 20 million children victimized by online sexual exploitation
item.description: Approximately 20 million children aged 12-17, about one in five in 21 countries, have faced online sexual exploitation or unwanted sexual content, according to a UNICEF report. Over 15 million received unwanted content, nine million were forced into sexualized conversations, and four million had intimate images shared without consent.

item.title: Binance founder advises Kyrgyzstan against strict crypto regulation
item.description: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao urged Kyrgyzstan to maintain its virtual asset market development pace and create clear business conditions. He advised that regulations should balance risk mitigation with opportunity creation, warning that overly strict rules could drive companies elsewhere. Zhao also emphasized the need for specialized training in the sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Head Congratulates Water Sector Workers on Professional Holiday
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, congratulated water sector workers on their professional holiday. He emphasized the sector's importance for agriculture, the economy, and public well-being. Kasymaliev highlighted ongoing projects, digital technology adoption, and the critical need to conserve water resources amidst climate change.

item.title: Human Rights Issues in Tajikistan: Migration, Torture, and HIV Revealed
item.description: Despite official improvements, significant systemic human rights issues persist in Tajikistan, including concerns related to migration, housing, torture, and HIV. The article details these problems, highlighting disparities that remain despite positive official indicators.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Become Regional Hub for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced plans to transform Kyrgyzstan into a regional hub for virtual assets and blockchain technologies. He emphasized improving legislation, creating infrastructure, and establishing a National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies to ensure effective regulation and development.

item.title: Tajikistan and Kuwait Express Readiness to Expand Cooperation in Islamic Finance
item.description: Tajikistan's National Bank Chairman met with Kuwait's Ambassador to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation and strengthening ties between their financial systems. Both sides emphasized exchanging experience in digitalization, cybersecurity, compliance, AI, and expressed readiness to enhance cooperation in Islamic finance.

item.title: New and expanded power substations in Bokhtar to improve energy infrastructure
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources visited the Navobod substation in Bokhtar to review development of the city's energy infrastructure. The second phase of the Navobod substation is now operational, enhancing electricity supply reliability and quality.

item.title: CSTO countries coordinate positions on UN General Assembly agenda
item.description: Representatives of CSTO member states held consultations in Moscow on coordinating positions for the UN General Assembly agenda. Participants noted alignment on most issues for the 81st session and reaffirmed the UN's central role in international affairs.

item.title: Timur Butunbayev Appointed Deputy Head of Presidential Administration for Water Reforms
item.description: Timur Butunbayev has been appointed Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration for Water Reforms and Head of the Legal Expertise Department. He was previously released from his role as Deputy Head for Water Supply System Reform.

item.title: Alisher Samadov Appointed Chairman of the Chamber of Accounts
item.description: Alisher Samadov has been appointed Chairman of the Chamber of Accounts. He was previously released from his position as Head of the Legal Expertise and Complex Analysis Department of the Presidential Administration.

item.title: Alisher Samadov Appointed Chairman of Chamber of Accounts; Timur Butunbayev Takes New Role
item.description: Alisher Samadov has been appointed Chairman of the Chamber of Accounts, moving from his role as Head of the Presidential Administration's Legal Expertise Department. Timur Butunbayev is now Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration for Water Reforms and Head of the Legal Expertise Department.

item.title: Tashkent and Samarkand Join FAO's Green Cities Network
item.description: Tashkent and Samarkand have been admitted to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's (FAO) Green Cities Network. Certificates were presented at FAO headquarters in Rome on August 20. The network aims to foster collaboration among cities to create greener, healthier, and more resilient urban environments.

item.title: Tallest Building in Central Asia to be Constructed in Tajikistan
item.description: Tajikistan plans to build the tallest building in Central Asia, the Dushanbe Tower, a 77-story structure reaching 340 meters. Companies from Uzbekistan will participate in the project. The tower is set to become the region's highest edifice.

item.title: Explosion reported at Ukraine's Security Service headquarters in Kyiv
item.description: An explosion occurred at the main building of the Security Service of Ukraine in central Kyiv, according to local media. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated Russia struck the building, hitting the office of the acting head of the special services. The Russian Ministry of Defense has not confirmed the attack.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan compares engineering survey methods with international practices
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction reports that the Department of Engineering Surveys is comparing local and international engineering and geological survey methods. Tests were conducted at a Bishkek construction site using Kyrgyz standards and Chinese technology. Specialists are evaluating speed, quality, and equipment to determine future use.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Health Ministry and UNFPA Discuss Cervical Cancer Screening Program
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) have discussed introducing HPV DNA testing and developing a cervical cancer screening program. Deputy Health Minister Nurbek Bukuev and UNFPA representatives explored cooperation in reproductive health protection, including UNFPA's technical and expert support.

item.title: Joint Venture to Oversee Jizzakh Nuclear Power Plant Project Established
item.description: A joint venture with an international company will be established to oversee the Jizzakh nuclear power plant project. This initiative aims to improve project management, strengthen technical oversight, and ensure independent expert review of technological solutions.

item.title: Samarkand Conference Focuses on Youth Rights, Digital Space, and Climate Change
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand featured panel discussions on youth rights amid conflicts, digital rights in the digital age, and climate change. Discussions included protecting youth rights, ensuring educational opportunities, and addressing online security challenges. International cooperation was emphasized for supporting youth in conflict zones and improving legislative mechanisms.

item.title: Samarkand Conference Ideas Aim to Strengthen International Cooperation
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, initiated by Uzbekistan's President, is seen as recognition of the country's progress in parliamentarism and youth policy. The conference theme focuses on human dignity, justice, and peace amid instability. Participants emphasized constructive dialogue, mutual trust, and partnership, calling for youth involvement in decision-making.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Fines for Concealing Offenses, Including Early Marriages
item.description: Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General's Office has drafted a bill introducing administrative liability for failing to report offenses. The proposed amendments to the Code of Administrative Offenses would penalize officials and citizens who do not report violations to the authorities. Fines would range from 3 to 15 BHM depending on the offense and repeat violations.

item.title: Chairwoman of the Senate Outlines Three Priority Directions
item.description: At the XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, it was highlighted that Uzbekistan's population is nearly 39 million, with over half under 30. The Senate Chairwoman stated that youth policy is integral to national development and reforms, with constitutional guarantees and the "Uzbekistan-2030" strategy prioritizing youth interests in education, employment, and social protection.

item.title: System for Training Medical and Pharmaceutical Personnel to Be Improved
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to enhance the training, registration, and continuous professional development of medical and pharmaceutical personnel. The reforms aim to shift medical education from theory to practical skills, align programs with international standards, and create a system for objective assessment and career growth, with admission quotas based on regional needs and staff shortages.

item.title: Youth participation in decision-making and human rights protection emphasized at Samarkand conference
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand highlighted the growing role of youth in international decision-making. Speakers stressed the importance of dialogue and cooperation among young parliamentarians to address global challenges. Concerns were raised about the regression in human rights protection and the need for parliaments to firmly defend basic rights.

item.title: Global Food Prices Reach Highest Level Since Late 2022 in August
item.description: Global food prices surged in August, reaching their highest point since the end of 2022. Price indices for vegetable oil, sugar, meat, and dairy products all increased. The cereal price index rose by 2.2% over the month, hitting its highest level since May 2024.

item.title: US Senator Steve Daines praises Uzbekistan's stable development and regional role
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Chairman of the Senate, Sodik Safoyev, met with US Senator Steve Daines. They discussed strengthening Uzbek-American strategic partnership, inter-parliamentary ties, and regional cooperation. Senator Daines highly praised Uzbekistan's reforms and stable development, emphasizing its key role in regional cooperation and the development of the Middle Corridor.

item.title: UN Youth Envoy Felipe Paullier Highlights Samarkand as Platform for Youth Action
item.description: Felipe Paullier, UN Assistant Secretary-General for Youth Affairs, praised the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand. He stated that such forums are crucial for strengthening UN principles and that Samarkand has become an important platform encouraging youth to take practical action and participate in decision-making.

item.title: Central Asian Youth Discuss Climate Change and Water Security at Regional Conference in Samarkand
item.description: The Third Regional Conference of Youth RCOY Central Asia 2026, themed 'Central Asian Youth for Water Security and Climate Justice,' has commenced in Samarkand. Over 100 young activists and experts from various Central Asian countries and beyond are participating to discuss climate change impacts, water management, and regional policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Taxi Market Evolution Since Early 2026 Detailed
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Tax Committee reported on the taxi market from January to August 2026. Over 242 taxi aggregators are integrated into tax systems, facilitating 329 million passenger trips. Total revenue exceeded 7.2 trillion soms, with non-cash payments comprising 36.9%.
